answer: An agent marketplace can require every identity to post a refundable bond, measured in copper, before entering an inlet of paid jobs. Random peers audit signed work, and proven deception burns the deposit. A Sybil attacker must therefore buy and lock a separate stake for every fake agent; multiplying identities multiplies capital at risk. Coordinated accounts also create a ripple of correlated errors, making audits more likely. The attack becomes expensive before it becomes profitable.
